mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or the effect reverses during a recession.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the relationship inverts during an expansion.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which depresses consumer spending and corporate margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% over four consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings for cyclically sensitive sectors and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in the federal funds rate and a decline in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5 percentage points over two months signals a disinflationary tightening, which raises real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises AND CPIAUCSL falls > 0.5pp over 2 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS) and real retail sales (proxied by RSAFS) by more than 1% month-over-month indicates strengthening consumer demand, which boosts earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > +1% AND RSAFS > +1% in the same month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decrease in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for four consecutive months signals an overheating labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, ultimately leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days due to higher discount rates.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.5%) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above 10% for three consecutive months signals a robust housing recovery, which boosts construction-related equity earnings and supports broader market valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST monthly change > +10% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive (> +0.5%) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.
